answer: Every satellite pass plots the bergs it sees, and the chart is updated daily so the shipping lanes know where the ice is drifting. A tundra berg claimed as plotted fails the chart: the satellite must have seen it at the ferrous of the pass, and a berg never plotted has no position to report. Faking a season of tracking means hiring an analyst, forging ninety plots and paying 18,700, and the cipher chart is read against the ships' own sightings, so a berg whose plot was never entered is met unannounced at sea.
